Auth.title: Your desk, one link away
Auth.lede: {app} is free for students. Sign in with your email — no password — to keep a watchlist, control your skills and ask people who do the work.

benefits.b1: A watchlist that remembers the filter you care about, and tells you when something moves.
benefits.b2: Skill suggestions from your degree and units — you confirm or remove every one.
benefits.b3: 20-minute coffee chats with practitioners who opted in to help.

Auth.free: Never paid for by employers. We don’t sell or share your data with them.
Auth.emailHint: We’ll email you a one-time sign-in link. Any email works; a uni address isn’t required.
Auth.ageHint: The service is for adults only.
Auth.privacyHint: What we collect, why, and who can see it — <link>read the privacy notice</link>.
Auth.googleNote: Google sign-in is simulated in this preview. The same two confirmations apply.
Auth.sentBody: We sent a sign-in link to {email}.
Auth.sentHint: It works once and expires in an hour. If it isn’t there in a minute, check spam.
Auth.previewBody: This preview doesn’t send email. The link sits in the preview outbox instead.
Auth.openPreview: Open the link from the preview outbox
Auth.signedOutBody: Your watchlist, skills and requests are saved for next time. The market stays open without an account.
Auth.deletedBody: Your profile, skills and watchlist were removed from view straight away. Everything else is permanently erased by {date}. We’ve emailed you a confirmation.

Onboarding.metaDescription: Three questions, ten seconds: see where your degree already puts you.
Onboarding.basicsKicker: About ten seconds · no account needed
Onboarding.basicsTitle: Three questions, then your starting point
Onboarding.basicsLede: We use your degree to suggest skills you probably have. They’re suggestions — you confirm or remove each one.
Onboarding.universityHint: Used to list your units and point to courses. Only you see it unless you share it with a practitioner.
Onboarding.degreeHint: Used to suggest skills your degree usually covers.
Onboarding.privacyNote: Before you sign up, these answers stay on this device. You can change or clear them any time.
Onboarding.skipped: Skipped — you can come back to this any time

board.firstBody: Tell us your degree and we’ll suggest where you already are. Until then, these are broad skills that open many doors and are quick to start.
board.suggestionNote: The figure on the right is Demand: how many Australian job ads mentioned the skill in the last four weeks. Suggestions aren’t saved as yours until you confirm them.

Onboarding.nextUnitsTitle: Add the units you’ve taken — about a minute
Onboarding.nextUnitsBody: Each unit sharpens your suggestions. Nothing is confirmed until you say so.
Onboarding.unitsLede: Tick what you’ve completed or are taking now. Each unit adds suggestions — you still confirm them.
Onboarding.unitsFrom: {n} units from {university}. More are added each semester.
Onboarding.noUnitMatch: No unit matches “{q}”. Try the code, like COMP2123.
Onboarding.unitsAdd: {n, plural, =0 {These refine what we already suggested.} one {Adds # new suggestion.} other {Adds # new suggestions.}}
Onboarding.unitsNone: Tick a unit to see what it adds.
Onboarding.noUnitsTitle: We don’t have the unit list for {university} yet
Onboarding.noUnitsBody: At launch we cover {launch}. Your degree already gives you a starting point, and you can add skills yourself any time.
Onboarding.doneEmptyLede: No answers, no problem. Here are broad first steps, and the market is open to browse.
Onboarding.savedBody: Confirm or remove the suggestions whenever you like.
Onboarding.saveTitle: Sign up to save your starting point
Onboarding.saveBody: Free, with just an email. Your answers come with you — and you can watch skills and ask people who use them.

Desk.title: Your desk
Desk.ledeSignals: {n, plural, one {One thing on your watchlist moved enough to flag.} other {# things on your watchlist moved enough to flag.}} Here’s what, and who to ask.
Desk.ledeQuiet: Nothing on your watchlist moved enough to flag. Here’s where things stand.
Desk.ledeEmpty: Start by watching a few skills or roles — we’ll tell you when they move.
Desk.setupBody: Tell us your degree and year and we’ll suggest skills you probably have.
Desk.signalsNone: No signals right now. We flag a change of at least 25% and 10 ads, with enough ads to trust it.
Desk.watchNote: Each item keeps the filter you added it with. “Since added” compares today with the day you added it.
Desk.heldEmpty: Mark skills you have as held to see how demand for them moves.
Desk.watchingEmpty: Nothing here yet — watch a skill or role from the market.
Desk.toHeld: Mark as a skill I have
Desk.editBody: Changing the filter restarts “since added” from today.
Desk.emptyBody: Watch a skill or role and we’ll show how it moves from the day you added it, with the filter you chose.
Desk.chatsWaitingNote: Replies can take a few days. If someone can’t make it, we quietly find someone else.
Desk.chatsEmpty: No chats yet. When something on the market catches your eye, ask someone who does the work.
Desk.chatDebriefHint: One tap — it helps the next student.
Desk.nextTitle: Pick a role to aim for
Desk.nextBody: We’ll compare it with your skills and suggest up to three next steps — with why, and how long they take.
Desk.nextRoleBody: Up to three priorities from what the role asks for, what you have, and how long each takes.

plain.toHeld: Mark as a skill I have

SkillsPage.title: What you bring, and what’s next
SkillsPage.lede: Suggestions come from your degree and units. Confirm what’s true, remove what isn’t — nothing here is a score, and nobody is compared with you.
SkillsPage.startingBody: You don’t need a long list to begin. Pick one of the first steps below, or tell us your degree to get suggestions.
SkillsPage.confirmedEmpty: Nothing confirmed yet. Add a skill you use, or confirm a suggestion.
SkillsPage.confirmedEmptyWithSuggestions: Confirm the suggestions that are true and they’ll move here.
SkillsPage.suggestedNote: Removing a suggestion deletes it — we keep no record of it and never use it to judge you.
SkillsPage.suggestedEmptyCta: Add your units to get more
SkillsPage.stepFirst: A common first step — broad and quick to start.
SkillsPage.stepAdjacent: Sits close to skills on your profile.
SkillsPage.stepRoles: {n, plural, one {Asked for in # role we track} other {Asked for in # roles we track}}; most in {role} ads ({pct}%).
SkillsPage.nextNote: Demand is one input. Effort and how widely a skill transfers matter as much.
SkillsPage.how1: Your degree and year give a first guess; each unit you tick adds evidence. We combine them and show a confidence — “Likely” from 70%, “Possibly” from 50%, otherwise “Maybe”.
SkillsPage.how2: A suggestion only becomes part of your profile when you confirm it. Practitioners see confirmed skills only, and only if you allow it in settings.
SkillsPage.how3: Next steps are skills often asked for together with yours, weighed by how quick they are to start and how widely they transfer.

Gap.title: Your next steps toward {role}
Gap.titleEmpty: Where do you want to head?
Gap.lede: Up to three priorities, each with why it matters and what it takes. A direction, not a checklist — and never a score.
Gap.ledeEmpty: Pick a role. We’ll compare what its ads ask for with your skills and suggest up to three next steps.
Gap.pickHint: You can change this any time; nothing is saved.
Gap.unknownRole: We don’t track that role yet. Choose one from the list.
Gap.haveNote: These are skills this role asks for that you already have.
Gap.haveNoteSuggested: Suggestions count as yours here — confirm or remove them on your skills page.
Gap.stepsTitle: {n, plural, one {Your next step toward {role}} other {Your next # steps toward {role}}}
Gap.stepsDoneTitle: You cover what this role asks for
Gap.coveredBody: Your profile covers the skills {role} ads ask for most. A chat with someone in the role is the best next step.
Gap.transferDetail: {n, plural, one {Asked for in # role we track} other {Asked for in # roles we track}}
Gap.waySourceIdea: Project idea — ours, not from a source
Gap.actTitle: Talk to someone who works as a {role}
Gap.actBody: Twenty minutes with someone who does the job will tell you which of these matters where you want to work.
Gap.talk: Talk to someone who does this
Gap.methodBody: Each missing skill is weighed by relevance (share of the role’s ads, {relevance}%), entry-level share of its ads ({entry}%), how widely it transfers ({transfer}%) and how quick it is to learn ({effort}%). Demand is one input, never the whole answer.

Settings.title: Your account
Settings.lede: Change what we know, who sees it, and what we send you. You can take your data with you or delete it.
Settings.profileLede: Only your name is needed. Everything else improves suggestions and is optional.
Settings.name: Name
Settings.nameHint: Shown to practitioners you request a chat with.
Settings.educationHint: Changing your education refreshes suggestions. Confirmed skills stay as they are.
Settings.visaHint: Private by default. Never shown to employers — we have no employer side.
Settings.visaWhyTitle: Why we ask, and why it’s optional
Settings.visaWhyBody: Some ads require permanent residency or citizenship. If you tell us your status we can default your filters to roles that don’t state that requirement, and a practitioner you choose to share it with can give more relevant advice. Leaving it blank changes nothing else.
Settings.profileSavedInference: Suggestions were refreshed from your education.
Settings.visibilityLede: For each field, choose whether only you see it or also practitioners you request a chat with. Nothing is ever shown publicly or to employers.

fieldHints.university: Helps a practitioner relate to your study.
fieldHints.year: Helps them pitch advice at the right stage.
fieldHints.skills: Suggestions are never shared — only skills you confirmed.
fieldHints.watchlist: Shows what you’re following, with its filters.
fieldHints.visa_status: Sensitive. Share only if it matters for your question.

visibility.matched_practitioner: Practitioners I request a chat with

Settings.visibilityNote: Practitioners only see a snapshot of what you allowed when you sent the request.
Settings.emailLede: Choose how often we write. Nothing marketing, ever.
Settings.digestHint: A short summary of what moved on your watchlist.
Settings.alertsHint: An email when something on your watchlist moves enough to flag. At most one a day.
Settings.transactionalTitle: Emails about your chat requests always come
Settings.transactionalBody: Confirmations, reminders and changes to a chat you booked are part of the service, so they can’t be switched off. Deleting your account stops them.
Settings.displayLede: How the product talks to you.

modeHints.market: Watchlist, held skills, signals — a light stock-market metaphor.
modeHints.plain: The same data in plain words: tracking, skills I have, changes.

Settings.themeHint: Starts out matching your device’s light or dark setting. Once you pick one, this browser remembers it.
Settings.dataLede: Your data is stored in Sydney, Australia. You can download it or delete it.
Settings.exportBody: A JSON file with your profile, skills, watchlist, chat requests and the emails we’ve sent you. We also email you when it’s ready.
Settings.exportDoneBody: We’ve also emailed you that an export was made.
Settings.deleteSummary: Removes your profile straight away and erases everything within {days} days.
Settings.deleteNow: Your profile, skills and watchlist are removed from view immediately and you are signed out.
Settings.deleteRequests: Open chat requests are cancelled so practitioners aren’t left waiting.
Settings.deletePurge: Everything, including backups, is permanently erased within {days} days.
Settings.deleteExportFirst: Want a copy? Download your data first.

effort.year_plus: A year or more to master

projects.languages: Build a small command-line tool in {skill} and publish it with a README.
projects.data: Take a public dataset (e.g. data.gov.au) and answer one real question with {skill}; write up what you found.
projects.web_product: Ship a small web app that uses {skill} and deploy it somewhere free.
projects.cloud_infrastructure: Deploy a tiny app on a free tier using {skill}, then write down how you’d tear it down and rebuild it.
projects.ways_of_working: Use {skill} deliberately in your next group project and note what changed.
projects.security: Work through a free {skill} lab or capture-the-flag and document your approach.
projects.default: Pick a small project that uses {skill} end to end and share what you learned.

StudentErrors.emailInvalid: Enter an email address like name@example.com.
StudentErrors.privacyRequired: Please confirm you’ve read the privacy notice.
StudentErrors.chooseOne: Choose one, or skip this step.
StudentErrors.nameRequired: Add the name you’d like practitioners to see.
StudentErrors.rateLimited: You’ve asked for 3 links in 10 minutes. Use the newest one, or wait a few minutes.
StudentErrors.linkInvalid: The link is incomplete or wasn’t issued by us. Request a new one.
StudentErrors.linkUsed: This link has already been used. Each link works once.
StudentErrors.linkExpired: This link has expired — links last one hour. Request a new one.
StudentErrors.skillAlreadyAdded: That skill is already on your profile.
StudentErrors.deleteConfirmMismatch: Type DELETE in capitals to confirm.
